I can only answer based on the document provided, which covers security deposits in Berkeley. The document does not contain information about rent caps, just cause eviction, application/screening fees, screening restrictions, or algorithmic pricing.

Based on the document, here are the operative security deposit obligations in Berkeley as of the retrieval date (2026-10-01):

## Security Deposit Limits

citations.cited_text:
Security deposit payments
Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons
Last month’s rent IS considered part of the security deposit
First month’s rent is NOT considered part of the security deposit
A California law,
Assembly Bill 12
, changed the amount landlords can charge as a security deposit to the amounts described above starting July 1, 2024.

content.text: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units. Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons.

citations.cited_text:
Landlord requirement to photograph unit before or at the start of a new tenancy
For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

content.text: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

citations.cited_text:
Move-out walk-through inspection requirement
Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning. This is to give tenants a chance to correct issues in order to avoid security deposit deductions.

content.text: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning, to give tenants a chance to correct issues in order to avoid security deposit deductions.

citations.cited_text:
Return of Security Deposit
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

content.text: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

citations.cited_text: If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions.

content.text: If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions.

citations.cited_text:
Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.
Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit. These photos and a written explanation of the cost of the repairs/cleaning must be given to the tenant along with the itemized statement.

content.text: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed. Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit. These photos and a written explanation of the cost of the repairs/cleaning must be given to the tenant along with the itemized statement.

citations.cited_text:
Security deposit interest
For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

content.text: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

citations.cited_text:
Security deposit deductions
A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to:
Cover rent default
Repair damages caused by a tenant or a tenant's guest other than normal wear and tear
Clean the unit to return it to the same level of cleanliness as at the start of the tenancy (for tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003)
If allowed by the lease, cover the cost of restoring or replacing personal property (including keys) or furniture, excluding ordinary wear and tear
The landlord cannot require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security deposit for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services, unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition it was in at the start of the tenancy, minus ordinary wear and tear.

content.text: A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to: cover rent default; repair damages caused by a tenant or a tenant's guest other than normal wear and tear; clean the unit to return it to the same level of cleanliness as at the start of the tenancy (for tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003); and if allowed by the lease, cover the cost of restoring or replacing personal property (including keys) or furniture, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
